target_customer: Smartphone owners who wanted to shoot and share video, plus brands and publishers using it for campaigns in 2012
problem: Capturing, editing and sharing phone video was clumsy; Socialcam aimed to be the Instagram of video and replace the default camera app.
business_model: Free consumer app aiming at scale; brand and publisher partnerships in 2012

founders.name: Michael Seibel
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia names him as a co-founder; the YC page lists only Luccisano and Bartram. Socialcam was spun out of Justin.tv in January 2012 per search results from press coverage.

founders.name: Guillaume Luccisano
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-founded Socialcam and later Triplebyte (S15) and Yuma (W23). Education not listed.

founders.name: Ammon Bartram
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and Wikipedia without background.

exit.reason: Autodesk 10-K says total cash consideration of 59.5 million dollars on August 1 2012; the app itself ended on 2015-10-28 per Wikipedia.

competitors.name: Viddy
competitors.what: Short video capture and sharing app limited to 15 seconds, the main Instagram for video rival

competitors.name: Instagram
competitors.what: Photo sharing app and the comparison benchmark after its 1 billion dollar Facebook sale in April 2012

competitors.name: Mobli
competitors.what: Mobile media sharing app that appeared in 2011

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile video capture, on the fly encoding and cross platform apps with Facebook integration were moderate engineering; scaling to millions of downloads in weeks was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Several rivals launched near identical apps, and growth leaned on Facebook sharing rather than a lasting network.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter's Vine launched in January 2013 and Instagram added video in June 2013 (not sourced here); Autodesk bought Socialcam in 2012 before that.

market_need_then: Smartphone video was booming in 2011 and 2012; Socialcam reported 4 million new users in one weekend in April 2012 and over 16 million downloads by July 2012, though growth was driven heavily by Facebook auto sharing.

branding.domain_note: Used socialcam.com, which failed to resolve from this session.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer friendly; a leaderboard and brand partner campaigns in 2012

branding.community_and_virality: Press focused on growth tactics and Facebook auto sharing spam complaints, which turned part of the brand perception negative in spring 2012.

brand_strength.rationale: The name was widely seen through Facebook auto posts but tech press tied it to spammy sharing; no mascot or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Socialcam spun out of Justin.tv, joined YC W12 and grew to over 16 million downloads by July 2012, largely through Facebook auto sharing, which drew spam complaints. Autodesk paid about 59.5 million dollars cash in August 2012. The app later ended on 28 October 2015 per Wikipedia, after brands left by late 2013. Platform dependency and Vine and Instagram video are plausible causes but no company statement gives a reason.
notes: The Autodesk deal was announced in July 2012 at 60 million dollars; the 10-K says 59.5 million cash closed August 1 2012. Seed amount conflicts: PitchBook shows 914K on 2012-03-27 and 2.59M total, CB Insights shows 20K; TechCrunch says amounts not disclosed, so amount left null. Wikipedia says the app launched March 2011 and ended October 2015, a shutdown after acquisition; status mismatch with Acquired is explained here. Website socialcam.com did not resolve. The founding story about the Justin.tv spin out comes from search summaries. Failure factors are inferred from press, not stated by the company; the Vine and Instagram video dates in takeover_risk_then are from general knowledge and unsourced.
